title: Painful gingival swelling in a 38-year-old man
html: A 38-year-old man came to the oral and maxillofacial surgery outpatient clinic at Columbia University, New York, New York, for evaluation of a left-sided gingival swelling. The patient reported pain and paresthesia of the left mandibular gingiva occurring for more than 1 month that started with bleeding in the area 5 months previously. His medical history was significant for idiopathic pancytopenia, atrial flutter, and cardiac tamponade. Clinical symptoms included fever, night sweats, and decreased appetite.
